subject: Mid-cycle request: bulk add-on discount and alignment
messages:
From: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@nexalabs.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@nexalabs.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-cycle add-on: bulk discount request

Hi Stephanie,

Quick note from our procurement/engineering sync this morning — we need to add an additional 500k generation tokens per month to support a new pilot (customer-facing feature launching in July). Given this is mid-contract and the usage will be sustained for at least six months, is there a standard bulk add-on discount or a mid-cycle amendment path you can recommend?

We attached our forecast for May–Nov to help you size. Key asks:
- Discount tiering for sustained add-ons (6+ months)
- Proration approach if we add now but want to co-term at annual renewal in Oct
- Any minimum commitment or lead time required from Redwood side

Appreciate a ballpark today so we can route internally — we have procurement review this week.

Thanks,
Carlos Ruiz
Head of Platform Operations
Nexa Labs

Attachment: Nexa_usage_forecast_May2027.xlsx
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@nexalabs.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@nexalabs.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle add-on: bulk discount request

Hi Carlos — thanks for the details and the forecast.

Short answer: yes, we can support a mid-cycle add-on with a graduated discount for sustained volumes, and we have two common paths depending on whether you want to: (A) keep the add-on on a month-to-month top-up with discounted unit rates, or (B) convert the add-on into a co-term amendment that annualizes the new capacity (which typically yields a deeper effective discount).

I can share a clean numbers example after I align internal approvals, but to set expectations:
- Month-to-month top-up: modest discount (5–12%) applied immediately, prorated for the remainder of the month. No minimum commitment beyond the add-on.
- Co-term annualize: deeper discount (12–25% effective depending on term length and committed units) if you convert now and annualize the new baseline at renewal in October. This will require a short amendment and signature (we can DocuSign).

Next steps: if you can confirm which path you prefer and whether the 500k/mo is expected to be recurring beyond Oct, I’ll run a quick finance check and share a draft amendment + ballpark numbers today.

Cc'ing our finance lead for visibility.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0193
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Nexa mid-cycle add-on — need pricing guidance

Hi team — forwarding Nexa's request. TL;DR: +500k gen tokens/month starting now, sustained for >=6 months, they want a mid-cycle discount and clarity on proration/co-term. Attached is their forecast.

Questions for finance/sales ops:
- For a six-month sustained add-on that we then annualize at renewal (Oct), what’s the widest range we can offer pre-approval? They asked for a ballpark today to move procurement.
- If we propose a split path (month-to-month discounted top-up now + option to annualize at renewal with credit toward signed amendment), what is the recommended discount schedule and any guardrails?

Suggested anchor from AE side: offer 15% effective if they commit to annualize in Oct (with a 9–12 month amortization window), or 8% if they remain month-to-month but sustain 3+ months. Is that reasonable?

Please reply with finance-approved thresholds and any legal/contract notes we should surface.

—Steph

Attachment: Nexa_usage_forecast_May2027.xlsx
From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 13:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Nexa mid-cycle add-on — need pricing guidance

Thanks for the flag — quick finance view below.

1) Ballpark pre-approval ranges (you can give Carlos today):
- Month-to-month sustained top-up (>=3 months): 7–9% off list unit price for token volumes between 250k–750k/mo.
- Convert-and-annualize at renewal: 14–18% effective discount if we annualize the new baseline and convert the remaining months into credit; the exact number depends on whether they lock a 12-month baseline or a minimum 9-month guaranteed conversion.

2) Proration approach: we will prorate the first-month invoice from the day of add-on activation; any months the add-on is active prior to the amendment can be applied as credit against the annualized baseline at the time of amendment (standard practice).

3) Legal / contract notes: we can do a one-page amendment (I recommend using the Draft-Amendment-Nexa.docx template) that:
- shows the new committed units,
- records the conversion credit formula (amount paid on top-ups to be credited pro rata toward annual baseline),
- sets a conversion window (we recommend Oct 1–Oct 31) for the co-term signature, and
- includes a rollback clause if usage falls below 60% of the new baseline for two consecutive quarters (protects Redwood).

4) Approval guardrails: Steph, you are pre-approved to offer up to 9% month-to-month and up to 16% effective for convert-and-annualize without exec signoff. Anything deeper routes to Ben/Revenue Ops.

If you want, I can draft the numbers and push a DocuSign today — I built a sample amendment with the two scenarios and attached it for review.

Attachment: Draft-Amendment-Nexa.docx

—David
Director, Revenue Finance
Redwood Inference
